chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether, from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Hammad from Al-Halby who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom I had advanced dirhams for foodstuff. So when my foodstuff was released to him, he sent the dirhams back to me and said: 'Buy food for yourself and fulfill your right.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that someone other than you should be put in charge of that, and you should stand with him until you take hold of that which is yours, and you should not rely upon yourself (alone) for its buying.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for securing one's financial right when advancing payment for goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practicalities of settling a debt paid in advance for goods, advising the creditor to appoint a third party to purchase the foodstuff while supervising the transaction to ensure the exact value is secured. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing ambiguity (*gharar*) and ensuring the precise fulfillment of rights in commercial exchanges, particularly when the debtor provides the means rather than the goods directly. It serves as a practical legal mechanism to safeguard the creditor's interest in informal or trust-based economic interactions.
